rationale: THE SITE CLASS THE OLD RULE LOST, PINNED — and the two forms a `hasError` test misreads. An `@include` whose mixin is NOT declared in the including file produced NO edge before 2026-10-23: the old code resolved the callee against the file's own mixin/function maps and returned when the name was absent, which MEASURED 1,995 of 2,205 clean `@include` sites (90%) on the whole admitted population. The 14-value campaign's `mixes_in` is now published for every COMPLETE include: a mixin named here and declared elsewhere is a real composition whose target is the written mixin name in the lane's published spelling (`@mixin <name>`); it is UNRESOLVED rather than absent, and the arbiter resolves it through the project index exactly as it resolves an `imports` specifier. The same-file case is still respelled to `<scope>::@mixin <name>` by publishScssFileScopedIdentities. THE LAST TWO ROWS ARE THE INSTRUMENT FIX: the first cut skipped any include whose subtree had `hasError`, which MEASURED 532 of 2,737 sites and wrongly included `@include f();` (an EMPTY argument list carries a MISSING token inside `arguments`) and `@include m { … }` (a CONTENT-BLOCK include can inherit an error from a nested rule). Completeness is the statement reaching its OWN terminator — `;` or a content block — and the census uses the same predicate, so the analyzer's emitted set and the measured site count cannot drift apart.

expectRelationships.note: THE PUBLISHED-BUT-UNRESOLVED ROW: the mixin's declaration is not in this file, so the target is the written name in the published spelling and carries mixinDeclaredInFile:false.
THE SAME-FILE CONTROL: the mixin IS declared here, so the target is respelled to the file-scoped identity.
THE EMPTY ARGUMENT LIST: `@include imported-empty();` is COMPLETE, but its `arguments` node carries a MISSING token, so a subtree `hasError` test skips it. This row pins that it publishes.
THE CONTENT-BLOCK FORM: `@include imported-content { … }` is a complete statement whose nested block can carry errors; a subtree `hasError` test skips it. This row pins that it publishes.
